abstracts.value: The differential cross section for <math altimg="si1.svg"><msup><mrow><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msup></math> production, measured as a function of the boson's transverse momentum (<math altimg="si2.svg"><msub><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></mrow></msub></math>), provides important constraints on the evolution of the transverse momentum dependent parton distribution functions (TMDs). The transverse single spin asymmetry (TSSA) of the <math altimg="si1.svg"><msup><mrow><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msup></math> is sensitive to one of the polarized TMDs, the Sivers function, which is predicted to have the opposite sign in <math altimg="si3.svg"><mi>p</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mo><mi>p</mi></math><math altimg="si4.svg"><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mo><mi>X</mi></math> from that which enters in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering. In this Letter, the STAR Collaboration reports the first measurement of the <math altimg="si5.svg"><msup><mrow><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><msup><mrow><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>⁎</mo></mrow></msup></math> differential cross section as a function of its <math altimg="si2.svg"><msub><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></mrow></msub></math> in <math altimg="si6.svg"><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em" linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mo><mi>p</mi></math> collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 510 GeV, together with the <math altimg="si5.svg"><msup><mrow><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><msup><mrow><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>⁎</mo></mrow></msup></math> total cross section. We also report the measurement of <math altimg="si5.svg"><msup><mrow><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><msup><mrow><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>⁎</mo></mrow></msup></math> TSSA in transversely polarized <math altimg="si6.svg"><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em" linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mo><mi>p</mi></math> collisions at 510 GeV.

The differential cross section for $Z^{0}$ production, measured as a function of the boson's transverse momentum ($p_{\mathrm{T}}$), provides important constraints on the evolution of the transverse momentum dependent parton distribution functions (TMDs). The transverse single spin asymmetry (TSSA) of the $Z^{0}$ is sensitive to one of the polarized TMDs, the Sivers function, which is predicted to have the opposite sign in $p+p$$\rightarrow W/Z+ X$ from that which enters in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering. In this Letter, the STAR Collaboration reports the first measurement of the $Z^{0}/\gamma^{*}$ differential cross section as a function of its $p_{\mathrm{T}}$ in $p$$+$$p$ collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 510 GeV, together with the $Z^{0}/\gamma^{*}$ total cross section. We also report the measurement of $Z^{0}/\gamma^{*}$ TSSA in transversely polarized $p$$+$$p$ collisions at 510 GeV.
